Based on the design of the key fob in your photo, this is a General Motors (GM) remote, typically used for vehicles like the Chevrolet Equinox, Silverado, or Malibu, as well as similar GMC or Buick models.

The short answer is yes, you can likely use your phone for these functions, but how you do it depends on the year of your car and your current service plan.

1. The Official Way: Manufacturer Apps

Since this is a GM fob, you can use the myChevrolet, myGMC, or myBuick app. These apps are designed to replicate the buttons on your fob:

  • Lock/Unlock: Can be done from almost anywhere with a cellular connection.
  • Remote Start: (The circle arrow icon) You can start your engine to pre-condition the cabin temperature.
  • Panic/Alarm: (The red icon) You can sound the horn/lights from the app.
  • Trunk/Liftgate: (The x2 icon) On equipped models, you can open the back hatch.

The Catch: These remote features usually require an active OnStar/Connected Services subscription (often called the "Remote Access" plan). If you bought the car used or your trial expired, you may need to pay a monthly fee to use the app for these functions.

2. The "Digital Key" (Phone-as-Key)

Newer models (typically 2024+) support Digital Key technology via Apple Wallet or Google Wallet.

  • How it works: Your phone uses Bluetooth or NFC to talk to the car. You don't even need to open an app; just walking up to the car unlocks it, and placing your phone on the wireless charger allows you to drive without the physical fob.
  • Compatibility: If your car is older (e.g., 2016–2022), it likely won't support "driving" with just the phone, even if the app can start the engine. You would still need the physical fob in your pocket to shift out of "Park."

3. Aftermarket Solutions

If your car doesn't support the official app or you want to avoid monthly fees, there are third-party systems like MoboKey or Viper SmartStart. These involve installing a small module in your car that connects to your phone via Bluetooth, allowing you to lock, unlock, and start the car through a separate app.

How to get started:

  1. Download the myChevrolet (or GMC/Buick) app.
  2. Create an account and enter your VIN (found on your registration or the corner of your dashboard).
  3. Check the "Remote Commands" section to see if your vehicle is compatible.

Yes, for a 2021 Chevy Malibu, you can definitely use your phone to perform all the functions shown on that key fob (and more).

Since your car is a 2021 model, it is fully equipped with the hardware needed for the myChevrolet mobile app. Here is exactly how to set it up and what you need to know about the cost.

Unlike a physical key fob which works for free, using your phone to control a 2021 Malibu requires an active OnStar / Connected Services plan.

3. What you can do from your phone:

Once the app is set up and the plan is active, you can:

  • Remote Start: Start the engine from anywhere (even miles away) to warm up or cool down the cabin.

Can I drive without the physical key?

It is possible to use the OBD2 port to add phone functionality to your 2021 Malibu, but there are some important distinctions to keep in mind regarding how "plug-and-play" these options actually are.

While most people use the OBD2 port for diagnostics (checking "Check Engine" lights), it can also be used as an entry point for vehicle control. Here are the three ways people typically use this for your car:

1. The Pro-Level DIY (OBD2 Bluetooth Adapters)

You can buy an OBD2 Bluetooth adapter (like the OBDLink MX+) and use a specialized app like Carista or OBD Fusion.

  • What it does: This is great for "customization." For some GM vehicles, you can use these to change settings, like making the windows roll down with the key fob or changing how the lights flash when you lock the car.
  • The Reality: While you can technically send a "lock" or "unlock" command through these apps, they are not designed for daily use as a key replacement. It’s clunky—you’d have to open the app, connect to Bluetooth, and navigate a menu every time you want to get in.

2. Aftermarket Smartphone Modules (The "Cleaner" Way)

Companies like MoboKey or Viper SmartStart offer modules that often interface with the car's wiring, sometimes using the OBD2 port for power or communication.

  • How it works: You (or a shop) install a small box under the dash.
  • The Benefit: These apps are built specifically to look like a key fob. Once installed, the app opens to a screen with the same buttons as your physical key.
  • Proximity Unlock: Some of these systems allow "Auto-Unlock," where the car unlocks just because your phone is in your pocket as you walk up—something the official Chevy app cannot do.

3. Key Programming (OBD2 for Setup Only)

If your goal is to have a backup, you can use an OBD2 programming tool (like those from Simple Key or Tom's Key Company) to "pair" a new physical fob or even a smartphone-based digital key to the car's computer.

  • You plug the programmer into the OBD2 port, follow the app's steps, and it "teaches" the car to recognize your phone or a new fob as a legitimate key.

Summary of Options for your 2021 Malibu

A Note on "Starting" the Car: Even with an OBD2 device, a 2021 Malibu still requires a physical security chip to be present to drive the car. Unless you install a high-end aftermarket system that "bypasses" the immobilizer, you can unlock and start the car with your phone, but you'll still need the physical key in the cup holder to shift into gear.

turns.prompt_text: how much would a professional installer cost
turns.response_html:
For a professional installation on a vehicle like your 2021 Chevy Malibu, costs typically range from $150 to $600 for labor alone, depending on the shop and the complexity of the hardware you choose.

If you are buying a complete system (hardware + labor), you can expect to pay between $400 and $800 for a mid-to-high-end smartphone-integrated setup.

Cost Breakdown by Service Type

Professional installers generally use two pricing models: flat-rate "packages" or hourly labor rates.

  • Flat-Rate Installation Packages: Many specialized shops (like Best Buy or local car audio specialists) offer bundles. For example, a Compustar 2-Way Remote Start System with professional installation included often retails for around $450 to $550.
  • Labor-Only (Customer Supplied Parts): If you buy your own module (like a Viper or DroneMobile unit) and bring it to a shop, they typically charge between $200 and $350 for the labor.
  • Hourly Rates: In areas like Ankeny, IA, the average hourly rate for a mobile electronics installer is approximately $22 to $30 per hour, but shops often charge a "shop rate" of $80 to $125 per hour to cover overhead and warranties.

Factors That Affect Your Price

Since your Malibu is a 2021 model, there are a few specifics that might move the price toward the higher end:

  • Bypass Modules: Newer GM vehicles require a specialized "bypass module" to communicate with the factory security system. This is often an extra $50 to $100 if not included in your kit.
  • T-Harness Wiring: Installers prefer using a "T-harness," which plugs directly into your car's existing wiring without cutting. This saves labor time but adds about $30 to $60 to the parts cost.
  • Smartphone Subscription: Remember that while the installation is a one-time cost, systems like Viper SmartStart or DroneMobile usually require a service plan (roughly $5 to $15 per month) to keep the LTE connection active.

Recommended "Installation Included" Options

Buying a bundle is often the most cost-effective way to get professional work with a warranty.

The Compustar 2-Way Remote Start System (CS4905S-KIT) is a popular all-in-one choice. It provides long-range remote start and can be upgraded with a smartphone module later if you decide you want app control.

Alternatively, the Viper SmartStart Pro is the gold standard for dedicated smartphone control. While hardware is sold separately, many shops offer it as a tiered "Advanced" installation because it involves GPS and LTE integration.

turns.prompt_text: how difficult would be installing a plug-in play harness
turns.response_html:
For a 2021 Chevy Malibu, installing a "Plug & Play" T-harness is generally considered a Low to Medium difficulty project. If you are comfortable removing a few plastic interior panels and plugging in connectors, you can likely finish it in 30 to 60 minutes.

Because your car is a 2021 model, most kits are designed to plug directly into the Body Control Module (BCM), which is usually located near the driver’s kick panel or under the steering column.

What Makes it "Plug & Play"?

In older cars, you had to cut and solder 15+ wires. With a T-harness, the process is simplified:

  • The T-Harness: You unplug a factory connector from your car, plug your new harness into that empty spot, and then plug the factory connector into the other end of your harness.
  • No Cutting: In most 2021 Malibu kits, zero wires need to be cut or spliced, which protects your car's factory warranty.

The Actual Steps (Malibu Specific)

  1. Panel Removal: You’ll use a pry tool to remove the plastic trim under the steering wheel or by your left foot to reach the wiring.
  2. Connection: You locate the matching colored plugs on the BCM and "T" into them with the harness.
  3. Programming: This is the most technical part. You usually have to plug the module into a Windows PC first to "flash" the firmware for a 2021 Malibu, then perform a "pairing" sequence in the car (e.g., clicking the ignition a certain number of times).
  4. Testing: Once the lights on the module turn green, you can test the remote start by pressing "Lock" three times on your original key fob.

Potential Roadblocks

  • Windows PC Requirement: Almost all these modules (Fortin, iDatalink, MPC) require a Windows computer and a specific USB link cable to setup the software before you plug it into the car.
  • Tight Spaces: The BCM can be tucked away, making it a bit of a "yoga move" to reach the plugs.
  • Ground Wire: Some "100% Plug & Play" kits still require you to screw one single "Ground" wire to a metal bolt on the car’s frame.

Recommended "Plug & Play" Kits for 2021 Malibu

The Start-X Remote Start Kit is highly rated for being one of the most "true" plug-and-play options for GM vehicles. It includes a pry tool and very clear, vehicle-specific video instructions that walk you through the Malibu dashboard.

The MPC Remote Start Kit is a great alternative that often comes pre-flashed, meaning you might be able to skip the computer setup step if you specify your vehicle year and model during checkout. It uses the same T-harness technology to keep installation clean.

Final Verdict: If you can put together IKEA furniture, you can likely handle this installation. It's much simpler than a traditional car stereo or alarm install.
